menu: main
---

There are many installation methods available for gomplate, depending on your platform and use-case.

## macOS/Linux with homebrew

The simplest method for macOS and Linux is to use [homebrew](https://brew.sh/):

```console
$ brew install gomplate
...

==> Installing gomplate
==> Pouring gomplate-3.8.0.x86_64_linux.bottle.tar.gz
🍺  /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/Cellar/gomplate/3.8.0: 6 files, 7.8MB
```

## Using mise-en-place on Linux/MacOS/Windows

If you are using [mise](https://github.com/jdx/mise), the polyglot tool version manager, you can use a command like this:

```console
mise use -g gomplate@latest
```

## macOS with MacPorts

On macOS, you can also install gomplate using [MacPorts](https://www.macports.org):

```console
$ sudo port install gomplate
```

## Windows with Chocolatey

The simplest method for installing gomplate on Windows is to use [`choco`](https://community.chocolatey.org/packages/gomplate):

```console
choco install gomplate
```

## Alpine Linux

`gomplate` is available in Alpine's `community` repository.

```console
$ apk add --no-cache gomplate
...
```

_Note: the Alpine version of gomplate may lag behind the latest release of gomplate._

## use with Docker

A simple way to get started is with one of the [hairyhenderson/gomplate][] Docker images.

```console
$ docker run hairyhenderson/gomplate:stable --version
gomplate version 3.9.0
```

Of course, there are some drawbacks - any files to be used for [datasources][]
must be mounted and any environment variables to be used must be passed through:

```console
$ echo 'My voice is my {{.Env.THING}}. {{(datasource "vault").value}}' | docker run -i -e THING=passport -v /home/me/.vault-token:/root/.vault-token hairyhenderson/gomplate -d vault=vault:///secret/sneakers -f -
My voice is my passport. Verify me.
```

It can be awkward to always type `docker run hairyhenderson/gomplate:stable`,
so this can be made simpler with a shell alias:

```console
$ alias gomplate='docker run hairyhenderson/gomplate:stable'
$ gomplate --version
gomplate version 3.9.0
```

### use inside a container

`gomplate` is often used inside Docker containers. When building images with Docker 17.05 or higher, you can use [multi-stage builds][] to easily include the `gomplate` binary in your container images.

Use the `COPY` instruction's `--from` flag to accomplish this:

```Dockerfile
...
COPY --from=hairyhenderson/gomplate:stable /gomplate /bin/gomplate
```

Now, `gomplate` will be available in the `/bin` directory inside the container image.

Note that when using `gomplate` with HTTPS-based datasources, you will likely need to install the `ca-certificates` package for your base distribution. Here's an example when using the [`alpine`](https://hub.docker.com/_/alpine) base image:

```Dockerfile
FROM alpine

COPY --from=hairyhenderson/gomplate:stable /gomplate /bin/gomplate
RUN apk add --no-cache ca-certificates
```

## manual install

1. Get the latest `gomplate` for your platform from the [releases][] page
2. Store the downloaded binary somewhere in your path as `gomplate` (or `gomplate.exe`
  on Windows)
3. Make sure it's executable (on Linux/macOS)
4. Test it out with `gomplate --help`!

In other words:

```console
$ curl -o /usr/local/bin/gomplate -sSL https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/download/<version>/gomplate_<os>-<arch>
$ chmod 755 /usr/local/bin/gomplate
$ gomplate --help
...
```

actions.command:
python3 - << 'PY' > /tmp/arity.txt
import json,re
d=json.load(open("/tmp/sigs.json"))
for k,(code,out,err) in d.items():
    if code==0:
        print(k, "OK0 type", out)
    else:
        try: e=json.loads(err)["err"]
        except: e=err
        m=re.search(r'wrong number of args for ([^:]+): ([^"]+)', e)
        if m: print(k, "arity", m.group(2))
        else:
            # strip prefix
            e=e.split('error calling')[-1][:220] if 'error calling' in e else e[:220]
            print(k, "OTHER", e)
PY
cat /tmp/arity.txt

package tmpl

import (
	"bytes"
	"fmt"
	"path/filepath"
	"text/template"
)

// Template is the tmpl namespace object.
type Template struct {
	root       *template.Template
	defaultCtx interface{}
	path       string
}

func New(root *template.Template, defaultCtx interface{}, path string) *Template {
	return &Template{root: root, defaultCtx: defaultCtx, path: path}
}

func (t *Template) SetRoot(root *template.Template) { t.root = root }

func (t *Template) Path() string { return t.path }

func (t *Template) PathDir() string { return filepath.Dir(t.path) }

// Exec executes a named template and returns output as string.
func (t *Template) Exec(name string, ctx ...interface{}) (string, error) {
	if t.root == nil || t.root.Lookup(name) == nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("template %q not defined", name)
	}
	var data interface{}
	if len(ctx) > 0 {
		data = ctx[0]
	}
	buf := &bytes.Buffer{}
	if err := t.root.ExecuteTemplate(buf, name, data); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return buf.String(), nil
}

// Inline renders a template string. Args are:
//   Inline in [context]
//   Inline name in [context]
func (t *Template) Inline(args ...interface{}) (string, error) {
	if len(args) == 0 || len(args) > 3 {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("wrong number of args for tpl: want 1, 2, or 3 - got %d", len(args))
	}
	var name, in string
	var data interface{} = t.defaultCtx
	switch len(args) {
	case 1:
		in = toString(args[0])
	case 2:
		name = toString(args[0])
		in = toString(args[1])
	case 3:
		name = toString(args[0])
		in = toString(args[1])
		data = args[2]
	}
	var tmpl *template.Template
	var err error
	if t.root != nil {
		tmpl = t.root.New(name)
		_, err = tmpl.Parse(in)
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
	} else {
		tmpl, err = template.New(name).Parse(in)
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
	}
	buf := &bytes.Buffer{}
	if err := tmpl.Execute(buf, data); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return buf.String(), nil
}

func toString(v interface{}) string {
	if s, ok := v.(string); ok {
		return s
	}
	return fmt.Sprint(v)
}

func JoinStrings(in interface{}, sep string) (string, error) {
	// in is expected to be slice/array; elements converted with toString
	if in == nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("input to Join must be an array: expected an array or slice, but got a reflect.Value")
	}
	rv := reflect.ValueOf(in)
	if rv.Kind() == reflect.String {
		// strings are not slices in original? Probe later
	}
	if rv.Kind() != reflect.Slice && rv.Kind() != reflect.Array {
		// Original may error differently; approximate with toString?
		// Check later via tests
		return "", fmt.Errorf("input to Join must be an array: expected an array or slice, but got a reflect.Value")
	}
	parts := make([]string, rv.Len())
	for i := 0; i < rv.Len(); i++ {
		parts[i] = toString(rv.Index(i).Interface())
	}
	return strings.Join(parts, sep), nil
}

package funcs

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/base64"
)

type Base64Funcs struct {
	ctx context.Context
}

func toBytes(in interface{}) []byte {
	switch v := in.(type) {
	case []byte:
		return v
	case string:
		return []byte(v)
	default:
		return []byte(toString(in))
	}
}

func (f *Base64Funcs) Encode(in interface{}) string {
	return base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(toBytes(in))
}

func decodeBase64(s string) ([]byte, error) {
	b, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(s)
	if err == nil {
		return b, nil
	}
	b2, err2 := base64.URLEncoding.DecodeString(s)
	if err2 == nil {
		return b2, nil
	}
	return nil, err
}

func (f *Base64Funcs) Decode(in string) (string, error) {
	b, err := decodeBase64(in)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return string(b), nil
}
func (f *Base64Funcs) DecodeBytes(in string) ([]byte, error) {
	return decodeBase64(in)
}
</output>

## `math.Div`

**Alias:** `div`

Divide the first number by the second. Division by zero is disallowed. The result will be a `float64`.

_Added in gomplate [v2.2.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v2.2.0)_
### Usage

```
math.Div a b
```
```
b | math.Div a
```

### Arguments

| name | description |
|------|-------------|
| `a` | _(required)_ The divisor |
| `b` | _(required)_ The dividend |

### Examples

```console
$ gomplate -i '{{ math.Div 8 2 }} {{ math.Div 3 2 }}'
4 1.5
```

## `math.Floor`

Returns the greatest integer value less than or equal to a given floating-point number. This wraps Go's [`math.Floor`](https://pkg.go.dev/math/#Floor).

**Note:** the return value of this function is a `float64` so that the special-cases `NaN` and `Inf` can be returned appropriately.

_Added in gomplate [v2.6.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v2.6.0)_
### Usage

```
math.Floor num
```

### Arguments

| name | description |
|------|-------------|
| `num` | _(required)_ The input number. Will be converted to a `float64`, or `0` if not convertible |

### Examples

```console
$ gomplate -i '{{ range (coll.Slice 5.1 42 "3.14" "0xFF" "NaN" "Inf" "-0") }}floor {{ printf "%#v" . }} = {{ math.Floor . }}{{"\n"}}{{ end }}'
floor 5.1 = 4
floor 42 = 42
floor "3.14" = 3
floor "0xFF" = 255
floor "NaN" = NaN
floor "Inf" = +Inf
floor "-0" = 0
```

## `math.IsFloat`

Returns whether or not the given number can be interpreted as a floating-point literal, as defined by the [Go language reference](https://golang.org/ref/spec#Floating-point_literals).

**Note:** If a decimal point is part of the input number, it will be considered a floating-point number, even if the decimal is `0`.

_Added in gomplate [v2.6.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v2.6.0)_
### Usage

```
math.IsFloat num
```

### Arguments

| name | description |
|------|-------------|
| `num` | _(required)_ The value to test |

### Examples

```console
$ gomplate -i '{{ range (coll.Slice 1.0 "-1.0" 5.1 42 "3.14" "foo" "0xFF" "NaN" "Inf" "-0") }}{{ if (math.IsFloat .) }}{{.}} is a float{{"\n"}}{{ end }}{{end}}'
1 is a float
-1.0 is a float
5.1 is a float
3.14 is a float
NaN is a float
Inf is a float
```

## `math.IsInt`

Returns whether or not the given number is an integer.

_Added in gomplate [v2.6.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v2.6.0)_
### Usage

```
math.IsInt num
```

### Arguments

| name | description |
|------|-------------|
| `num` | _(required)_ The value to test |

### Examples

```console
$ gomplate -i '{{ range (coll.Slice 1.0 "-1.0" 5.1 42 "3.14" "foo" "0xFF" "NaN" "Inf" "-0") }}{{ if (math.IsInt .) }}{{.}} is an integer{{"\n"}}{{ end }}{{end}}'
42 is an integer
0xFF is an integer
-0 is an integer
```

## `math.IsNum`

Returns whether the given input is a number. Useful for `if` conditions.

_Added in gomplate [v2.6.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v2.6.0)_
### Usage

```
math.IsNum in
```

### Arguments

| name | description |
|------|-------------|
| `in` | _(required)_ The value to test |

### Examples

```console
$ gomplate -i '{{ math.IsNum "foo" }} {{ math.IsNum 0xDeadBeef }}'
false true
```

## `crypto.ECDSAGenerateKey` _(experimental)_
**Experimental:** This function is [_experimental_][experimental] and may be enabled with the [`--experimental`][experimental] flag.

[experimental]: ../config/#experimental

Generate a new Elliptic Curve Private Key and output in
PEM-encoded PKCS#1 ASN.1 DER form.

Go's standard NIST P-224, P-256, P-384, and P-521 elliptic curves are all
supported.

Default curve is P-256 and can be overridden with the optional `curve`
parameter.

_Added in gomplate [v3.11.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.11.0)_
### Usage

```
crypto.ECDSAGenerateKey [curve]
```
```
curve | crypto.ECDSAGenerateKey
```

### Arguments

| name | description |
|------|-------------|
| `curve` | _(optional)_ One of Go's standard NIST curves, P-224, P-256, P-384, or P-521 -
defaults to P-256.
 |

### Examples

```console
$ gomplate -i '{{ crypto.ECDSAGenerateKey }}'
-----BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY-----
...
```

// Config holds gomplate configuration. Field order matters for YAML dumps.
type Config struct {
	Datasources       map[string]config.DataSource `yaml:"datasources,omitempty"`
	Context           map[string]config.DataSource `yaml:"context,omitempty"`
	Templates         map[string]config.DataSource `yaml:"templates,omitempty"`
	Plugins           map[string]PluginConfig      `yaml:"plugins,omitempty"`
	In                string                       `yaml:"in,omitempty"`
	InputDir          string                       `yaml:"inputDir,omitempty"`
	Excludes          []string                     `yaml:"excludes,omitempty"`

	OutputMap         string                       `yaml:"outputMap,omitempty"`
	OutputFiles       []string                     `yaml:"outputFiles,omitempty"`
	Chmod             string                       `yaml:"chmod,omitempty"`
	LeftDelim         string                       `yaml:"leftDelim,omitempty"`
	RightDelim        string                       `yaml:"rightDelim,omitempty"`
	MissingKey        string                       `yaml:"missingKey,omitempty"`

	PluginTimeout     time.Duration                `yaml:"pluginTimeout,omitempty"`
	ExecPipe          bool                         `yaml:"execPipe,omitempty"`
	Experimental      bool                         `yaml:"experimental,omitempty"`

	extraHeaders map[string]http.Header
}

func (c *Config) String() string {
	out, _ := yaml.Marshal(c)
	return string(out)
}

// PluginConfig configures a plugin.
type PluginConfig struct {
	Cmd     string        `yaml:"cmd"`
	Args    []string      `yaml:"args,omitempty"`
	Timeout time.Duration `yaml:"timeout,omitempty"`

def snapshot(root):

  elif p.is_file(): out[rel]=("file",oct(p.stat().st_mode&0o777),p.read_bytes())
 return out

func parseConstraintGroup(s string) ([]constraint, error) {
	// Split by commas not inside? simple, then tokens by whitespace merge operators
	s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
	if s == "" {
		return []constraint{{op: "*"}}, nil
	}
	// Split hyphen range "1.2 - 2.0" or "1.2-2.0" (complicated because prerelease hyphens)
	// Handle explicit " - " separator first
	if strings.Contains(s, " - ") {
		parts := strings.SplitN(s, " - ", 2)
		lo, err := NewVersion(strings.TrimSpace(parts[0]))
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		hi, err := NewVersion(strings.TrimSpace(parts[1]))
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		return []constraint{{op: ">=", v: lo}, {op: "<=", v: hi}}, nil
	}
	var cons []constraint
	for _, part := range strings.Split(s, ",") {
		part = strings.TrimSpace(part)
		if part == "" {
			continue
		}
		// part may contain space separated multiple constraints like ">= 1.0 < 2.0" or ">=1.0 <2.0"
		toks := tokenizeConstraint(part)
		for _, tok := range toks {
			c, err := parseOneConstraint(tok)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			cons = append(cons, c...)
		}
	}
	if len(cons) == 0 {
		cons = append(cons, constraint{op: "*"})
	}
	return cons, nil
}

		f := fields[i]
		if isOperator(f) && i+1 < len(fields) {
			out = append(out, f+fields[i+1])
			i++
		} else {
			out = append(out, f)
		}
	}
	return out
}

	switch s {

	}

func (f *CryptoFuncs) ECDSAGenerateKey(args ...interface{}) (string, error) {
	if err := checkExperimental(f.ctx); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	curveName := "P-256"
	if len(args) > 0 {
		curveName = toString(args[0])
	}
	var curve elliptic.Curve
	switch curveName {
	case "P-224":
		curve = elliptic.P224()
	case "P-256":
		curve = elliptic.P256()
	case "P-384":
		curve = elliptic.P384()
	case "P-521":
		curve = elliptic.P521()
	default:
		return "", fmt.Errorf("invalid curve %s", curveName)
	}
	key, err := ecdsa.GenerateKey(curve, rand.Reader)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	der, err := x509.MarshalECPrivateKey(key)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return string(pem.EncodeToMemory(&pem.Block{Type: "EC PRIVATE KEY", Bytes: der})), nil
}

func cueUnify(a, b interface{}) (interface{}, error) {
	// If either is cueRef unresolved, cannot check yet - prefer concrete b? Keep a and let resolve compare later - simplify return b if one is ref
	if _, ok := a.(cueRef); ok {
		return b, nil
	}
	if _, ok := b.(cueRef); ok {
		return a, nil
	}
	if fmt.Sprintf("%#v", a) == fmt.Sprintf("%#v", b) {
		return a, nil
	}
	am, ok1 := a.(map[string]interface{})
	bm, ok2 := b.(map[string]interface{})
	if ok1 && ok2 {
		out := make(map[string]interface{})
		for k, v := range am {
			out[k] = v
		}
		for k, v := range bm {
			if err := cueSetField(out, k, v); err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
		}
		return out, nil
	}
	return nil, fmt.Errorf("conflicting values")
}
func (p *cueParser) consumeSeparators() {
	for {
		p.skipInlineSpace()
		if p.peek() == ',' || p.peek() == ';' {
			p.pos++
			continue
		}
		// prevent self reference loops when field resolves to itself (same ref)
		cur2, err := resolveCueRefs(cur, scope, root)
		if err != nil {
			// reference errors in CUE are prefixed with field context by caller? Our parse wrapping at root does not add field - original error: "a: reference \"b\" not found" for field a referencing b.
			// That prefix is added when resolving struct fields in resolveStruct below - here just return err.
			return nil, err
		}
		cur = cur2
		for _, seg := range x.path[1:] {
			if m, ok := cur.(map[string]interface{}); ok {
				fv, ok := m[seg]
				if !ok {
					return nil, fmt.Errorf("field %q not found", seg)
				}
				cur = fv
			} else {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("cannot access field %s", seg)
			}
		}
		return cur, nil
	case map[string]interface{}:
		// This map is a struct scope - create child scope based on its fields for resolution of nested refs
		child := &cueScope{fields: x, parent: scope}
		out := make(map[string]interface{}, len(x))
		for k, val := range x {
			rv, err := resolveCueRefs(val, child, root)
			if err != nil {
				// Prefix with field name if not already
				msg := err.Error()
				if strings.Contains(msg, "reference") && !strings.HasPrefix(msg, k+":") {
					return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: %s", k, msg)
				}
				return nil, err
			}
			out[k] = rv
		}
		return out, nil
	case []interface{}:
		out := make([]interface{}, len(x))
		for i, el := range x {
			rv, err := resolveCueRefs(el, scope, root)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			out[i] = rv
		}
		return out, nil
	default:
		return v, nil
	}

// legacyArgs validation has the following behaviour:
// - root commands with no subcommands can take arbitrary arguments
// - root commands with subcommands will do subcommand validity checking
// - subcommands will always accept arbitrary arguments
func legacyArgs(cmd *Command, args []string) error {
	// no subcommand, always take args
	if !cmd.HasSubCommands() {
		return nil
	}

	// root command with subcommands, do subcommand checking.
	if !cmd.HasParent() && len(args) > 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("unknown command %q for %q%s", args[0], cmd.CommandPath(), cmd.findSuggestions(args[0]))
	}
	return nil

	if len(args) > 0 {

	if len(cmd.ValidArgs) > 0 {

// Find the target command given the args and command tree
// Meant to be run on the highest node. Only searches down.
func (c *Command) Find(args []string) (*Command, []string, error) {
	var innerfind func(*Command, []string) (*Command, []string)

	innerfind = func(c *Command, innerArgs []string) (*Command, []string) {
		argsWOflags := stripFlags(innerArgs, c)
		if len(argsWOflags) == 0 {
			return c, innerArgs
		}
		nextSubCmd := argsWOflags[0]

		cmd := c.findNext(nextSubCmd)
		if cmd != nil {
			return innerfind(cmd, c.argsMinusFirstX(innerArgs, nextSubCmd))
		}
		return c, innerArgs
	}

	commandFound, a := innerfind(c, args)
	if commandFound.Args == nil {
		return commandFound, a, legacyArgs(commandFound, stripFlags(a, commandFound))
	}
	return commandFound, a, nil
}

func (c *Command) findSuggestions(arg string) string {
	if c.DisableSuggestions {
		return ""
	}
	if c.SuggestionsMinimumDistance <= 0 {
		c.SuggestionsMinimumDistance = 2
	}
	var sb strings.Builder
	if suggestions := c.SuggestionsFor(arg); len(suggestions) > 0 {
		sb.WriteString("\n\nDid you mean this?\n")
		for _, s := range suggestions {
			_, _ = fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "\t%v\n", s)
		}
	}
	return sb.String()
}

package gomplate

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"time"

	"example.com/gomplate/internal/logging"
)

type renderer struct {
	cfg               *Config
	templatesRendered int
	errors            int
	duration          time.Duration
	registry          *dsRegistry
}

// Run renders templates according to cfg.
func Run(ctx context.Context, cfg *Config) error {
	r := &renderer{cfg: cfg}
	state := logging.FromContext(ctx)
	defer func() {
		// completed rendering is logged even on error paths after Run is entered
		logging.FromContext(ctx).Logger.Debug("completed rendering", "templatesRendered", r.templatesRendered, "errors", r.errors, "duration", r.duration)
		_ = state
	}()
	if err := cfg.validate(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if cfg.Experimental {
		logging.SetExperimental(ctx)
		logging.Logger(ctx).Info("experimental functions and features enabled!")
	}
	ioCtx := IOFromContext(ctx)
	r.registry = newDSRegistry(cfg, ioCtx.Stdin)
	// create context from context datasources
	dataCtx, err := r.createContext(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return r.RenderTemplates(ctx, dataCtx)
}

func (r *renderer) createContext(ctx context.Context) (interface{}, error) {
	tctx := make(tmplctx)
	var root interface{}
	rootSet := false
	// Iterate map in Go random order to match original error non-determinism
	for alias := range r.cfg.Context {
		v, err := r.registry.readParsed(ctx, alias)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		if alias == "." {
			root = v
			rootSet = true
		} else {
			tctx[alias] = v
		}
	}
	if rootSet {
		return root, nil
	}
	return &tctx, nil
}

func (r *renderer) RenderTemplates(ctx context.Context, dataCtx interface{}) error {
	ioCtx := IOFromContext(ctx)
	templates, err := r.gatherTemplatesForRender(ctx, ioCtx, dataCtx)
	if err != nil {
		r.errors++
		return fmt.Errorf("failed to gather templates for rendering: %w", err)
	}
	return r.renderTemplatesWithData(ctx, templates, dataCtx)
}

func (r *renderer) gatherTemplatesForRender(ctx context.Context, ioCtx IO, dataCtx interface{}) ([]tmplData, error) {
	templates, err := gatherTemplates(ioCtx, r.cfg, r)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	// Fill outputs for input-dir mode
	if r.cfg.InputDir != "" {
		for i := range templates {
			if r.cfg.OutputMap != "" {
				out, err := r.renderOutputMap(ctx, templates[i].name, dataCtx)
				if err != nil {
					return nil, fmt.Errorf("walkDir: %w", err)
				}
				templates[i].output = out
			} else {
				templates[i].output = joinOutput(r.cfg.OutputDir, templates[i].name)
			}
		}
	}
	return templates, nil
}

func joinOutput(dir, rel string) string {
	if dir == "" || dir == "." {
		return rel
	}
	// Use filepath join but preserve forward slashes in rel
	// templates name is slash path
	return dir + "/" + rel
}

func displayForError(alias string, ds config.DataSource, final *url.URL, args []string) string {
	return alias
}
func displayURLForError(ds config.DataSource, final *url.URL, args []string) string {
	if len(args) == 0 {
		if ds.URL == nil { return "" }
		return stripTypeParam(ds.URL).String()
	}
	return stripTypeParam(final).String()
}
func stripTypeParam(u *url.URL) *url.URL {
	if u == nil { return u }
	clone := *u
	typeParam := os.Getenv("GOMPLATE_TYPE_PARAM")
	if typeParam == "" { typeParam = "type" }
	if clone.Query().Has(typeParam) {
		q := clone.Query(); q.Del(typeParam); clone.RawQuery = q.Encode()
	}
	return &clone
}

func (r *dsRegistry) readInclude(ctx context.Context, alias string, args ...string) (string, error) {
	ds, _, err := r.lookup(alias)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	finalURL := joinURL(ds.URL, args)
	if finalURL.Scheme == "merge" {
		v, err := r.readMerge(ctx, alias, ds, finalURL)
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		// include merge result as JSON? Original merge FS returns bytes of merged JSON maybe
		b, _ := json.Marshal(v)
		return string(b), nil
	}
	raw, err := r.readRaw(ctx, alias, ds, finalURL)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("couldn't read datasource '%s' (%s): %w", alias, displayURLForError(ds, finalURL, args), err)
	}
	if raw.isDir {
		// include of a directory: original likely errors reading dir. The raw reading
		// would have open/read a directory - for local, readRaw detects dir and lists.
		// For include, return ??? test later
		return strings.Join(raw.entries, "\n"), nil
	}
	return string(raw.data), nil
}

func (r *dsRegistry) readRaw(ctx context.Context, alias string, ds config.DataSource, finalURL *url.URL) (*rawResult, error) {
	cacheKey := alias + "\x00" + finalURL.String()
	if cached, ok := r.rawCache[cacheKey]; ok {
		if cached.err != nil {
			return nil, cached.err
		}
		return cached, nil
	}
	res, err := r.readRawUncached(ctx, alias, ds, finalURL)
	// Cache successes and stdin? Cache all to preserve stdin consumption per alias/url
	if err != nil {
		// Don't cache other errors? Stdin empty returns success so fine.
		return nil, err
	}
	r.rawCache[cacheKey] = res
	return res, nil
}

```console

```

This will cause only files ending in `.tmpl` to be processed, except for files with names beginning with `foo`: `template.tmpl` will be included, but `foo-template.tmpl` will not.

### `--exclude-processing`

When using the [`--input-dir`](#--input-dir-and---output-dir) argument, it can be useful to skip some files from processing and copy them directly to the output directory. Like the `--exclude` flag, it takes a [`.gitignore`][]-style pattern, and any files match the pattern will be copied.

_Note:_ These patterns are _not_ treated as filesystem globs, and so a pattern like `/foo/bar.json` will match relative to the input directory, not the root of the filesystem as they may appear!

Examples:

```console
$ gomplate --exclude-processing '*.png' --input-dir in/ --output-dir out/
```

This will skip all `*.png` files in the `in/` directory from being processed, and copy them to the `out/` directory.

#### `.gomplateignore` files

You can also use a file named `.gomplateignore` containing one exclude pattern on each line. This has the same syntax as a [`.gitignore`][] file.
When processing sub-directories, `.gomplateignore` files in the parent directory are also considered. Patterns are matched relative to the location of the `.gomplateignore` file.

### `--datasource`/`-d`

Add a data source in `name=URL` form. Specify multiple times to add multiple sources. The data can then be used by the [`datasource`](../functions/data/#datasource) and [`include`](../functions/data/#include) functions.

Data sources referenced in this way are lazy-loaded: they will not be read until the template is parsed and a `datasource` or `include` function is encountered.

See [Datasources](../datasources) for full details.

A few different forms are valid:

- `mydata=file:///tmp/my/file.json`
  - Create a data source named `mydata` which is read from `/tmp/my/file.json`. This form is valid for any file in any path.
- `mydata=file.json`
  - Create a data source named `mydata` which is read from `file.json` (in the current working directory). This form is only valid for files in the current directory.
- `mydata.json`
  - This form infers the name from the file name (without extension). Only valid for files in the current directory.

type tmplData struct {
	name     string
	contents string
	output   string
	mode     os.FileMode
	noParse  bool // exclude-processing copy
	// raw bytes for noParse
	raw []byte
}

func parseChmod(cfg *Config) (os.FileMode, error) {
	if cfg.Chmod == "" {
		return 0, nil
	}
	v, err := strconv.ParseUint("0"+cfg.Chmod, 8, 32)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	return os.FileMode(v), nil
}

func gatherTemplates(ctxIO IO, cfg *Config, r *renderer) ([]tmplData, error) {
	chmod, err := parseChmod(cfg)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err

		if chmod != 0 {
			return chmod
		}
		return def

				out = cfg.OutputFiles[0]
			}
			return []tmplData{{name: "<arg>", contents: cfg.In, output: out, mode: chmodApply(0o644)}}, nil
		}
	}
	if cfg.InputDir != "" {
		return gatherFromDir(ctxIO, cfg, r, chmodApply)
	}
	// InputFiles
	var out []tmplData
	for i, inFile := range cfg.InputFiles {
		outFile := cfg.OutputFiles[i] // may panic for execPipe multi, matching original

func jqCombinations(c *jqCtx, argNodes []jqNode, in interface{}) ([]interface{}, error) {
	var sources [][]interface{}
	if len(argNodes) > 0 {
		for _, an := range argNodes {
			vals, err := an.eval(c, in)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			if len(vals) > 0 {
				if arr, ok := vals[0].([]interface{}); ok {
					sources = append(sources, arr)
				}
			}
		}
	} else {
		arr, ok := in.([]interface{})
		if !ok {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("combinations cannot be applied to: %s", jqPreview(in))
		}
		for _, el := range arr {
			if sub, ok := el.([]interface{}); ok {
				sources = append(sources, sub)
			} else {
				sources = append(sources, []interface{}{el})
			}
		}
	}
	results := [][]interface{}{{}}
	for _, src := range sources {
		var nr [][]interface{}
		for _, base := range results {
			for _, el := range src {
				nr = append(nr, append(append([]interface{}{}, base...), el))
			}
		}
		results = nr
	}
	out := make([]interface{}, len(results))
	for i, r := range results {
		out[i] = r
	}
	return out, nil

func (f *NetFuncs) CIDRSubnets(newbitsArg interface{}, prefixArg interface{}) ([]netip.Prefix, error) {
	if err := checkExperimental(f.ctx); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	prefix, err := parsePrefixArg(prefixArg)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	nb, err := toInt64(newbitsArg)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	newBits := prefix.Bits() + int(nb)
	if nb < 0 || newBits > prefix.Addr().BitLen() {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("newbits %d out of range", nb)
	}
	count := 1 << uint(nb)
	out := make([]netip.Prefix, 0, count)
	base := prefix.Masked().Addr()
	// step = 2^(addrBits-newBits)
	hostBits := prefix.Addr().BitLen() - newBits
	for i := 0; i < count; i++ {
		var addr netip.Addr
		if hostBits >= 64 {
			// large IPv6 subnets: add i << hostBits via generic big add
			addr = addShifted(base, uint64(i), uint(hostBits))
		} else {
			addr = addToAddr(base, uint64(i)<<uint(hostBits))
		}
		out = append(out, netip.PrefixFrom(addr, newBits))
	}
	return out, nil
}

func addShifted(base netip.Addr, v uint64, shift uint) netip.Addr {
	// add v << shift to base address (big-endian)
	if base.Is4() {
		arr := base.As4()
		// convert to uint32
		n := uint32(arr[0])<<24 | uint32(arr[1])<<16 | uint32(arr[2])<<8 | uint32(arr[3])
		n += uint32(v << shift)
		return netip.AddrFrom4([4]byte{byte(n >> 24), byte(n >> 16), byte(n >> 8), byte(n)})
	}
	arr := base.As16()
	// add as big integer in bytes
	// compute total bit offset from right
	carry := uint64(0)
	// We add v at byte position from right = shift/8, bit shift%8
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		byteFromRight := i
		idx := 15 - i
		var add uint64
		if uint(byteFromRight)*8 >= shift && uint(byteFromRight)*8 < shift+64 {
			offset := uint(byteFromRight)*8 - shift
			if offset < 64 {
				add = (v >> offset) & 0xff
			}
			// plus bits from lower byte crossing? v>>offset captures appropriate bits for this byte when shift%8 !=0, need combine
			if shift%8 != 0 && offset > 0 {
				// already shifted accordingly? Complex; fallback handled by generic below
			}
		}
		_ = add
		_ = idx
		_ = carry
		break
	}
	// Simpler: use netip Next repeatedly not feasible. Use manual big-int via bits in a 16-byte array
	// Implement addition of v<<shift using byte array of the value in big endian 16 bytes
	var val [16]byte
	// place v bits starting at 'shift' from right
	for b := 0; b < 64; b++ {
		if (v>>uint(b))&1 == 1 {
			pos := shift + uint(b) // from right, 0-index
			byteIdx := 15 - int(pos/8)
			if byteIdx >= 0 {
				val[byteIdx] |= 1 << (pos % 8)
			}
		}
	}
	carry16 := 0
	for i := 15; i >= 0; i-- {
		sum := int(arr[i]) + int(val[i]) + carry16
		arr[i] = byte(sum & 0xff)
		carry16 = sum >> 8
	}
	_ = bits.OnesCount
	return netip.AddrFrom16(arr)
}

func (f *NetFuncs) CIDRSubnetSizes(args ...interface{}) ([]netip.Prefix, error) {
	if err := checkExperimental(f.ctx); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	// signature in original produces custom error for <2 args, but our variadic template
	// error for 0 args must be custom. If Go template calls with 0, this runs.
	if len(args) < 2 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("wrong number of args: want 2 or more, got %d", len(args))
	}
	prefix, err := parsePrefixArg(args[len(args)-1])
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	base := prefix.Masked().Addr()
	cur := base
	out := make([]netip.Prefix, 0, len(args)-1)
	for _, a := range args[:len(args)-1] {
		nb, err := toInt64(a)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		newBits := prefix.Bits() + int(nb)
		if nb < 0 || newBits > prefix.Addr().BitLen() {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("newbits %d out of range", nb)
		}
		p := netip.PrefixFrom(cur, newBits)
		// Terraform cidrsubnets aligns cur to next boundary of this prefix size if needed
		p = p.Masked()
		if p.Addr() != cur {
			// advance cur to next aligned boundary: add size of one prefix to masked
			size := subnetSize(p)
			cur = addToAddr(p.Addr(), size)
			p = netip.PrefixFrom(cur, newBits).Masked()
		}
		out = append(out, p)
		cur = addToAddr(p.Addr(), subnetSize(p))
	}
	return out, nil
}

func subnetSize(p netip.Prefix) uint64 {
	hostBits := p.Addr().BitLen() - p.Bits()
	if hostBits >= 64 {
		return 0
	} // not handled for huge IPv6 in this helper
	return uint64(1) << uint(hostBits)
}

// matchPattern matches gitignore/doublestar-ish patterns against a slash path.
func matchPattern(pattern, rel string) bool {
	if pattern == "" {
		return false
	}
	if strings.HasSuffix(pattern, "/") {
		// Directory-only patterns are matched only against directories in original walk;
		// we are called on files, so they never match here.
		return false
	}
	anchored := strings.Contains(pattern, "/")
	pat := strings.TrimPrefix(pattern, "/")
	// A segment containing ** but not exactly ** is an invalid doublestar pattern and matches nothing
	for _, seg := range strings.Split(pat, "/") {
		if strings.Contains(seg, "**") && seg != "**" {
			return false
		}
		if _, err := path.Match(seg, ""); err != nil {
			return false
		}
	}
	segs := strings.Split(rel, "/")
	if !anchored {
		// Match any single path segment
		for _, seg := range segs {
			if ok, _ := path.Match(pat, seg); ok {
				return true
			}
		}
		return false
	}
	// Anchored: whole path or any leading prefix (directory prefix)
	if doublestarMatch(pat, rel) {
		return true
	}
	for i := 1; i < len(segs); i++ {
		if doublestarMatch(pat, strings.Join(segs[:i], "/")) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

func matchedExclude(rel string, full string, rootAbs string, patterns []string) bool {
	excluded := false
	for _, p := range patterns {
		neg := false
		pat := p
		if strings.HasPrefix(pat, "!") {
			neg = true
			pat = pat[1:]
		}
		if matchPattern(pat, rel) {
			excluded = !neg
		}
	}
	if excluded {
		return true
	}
	// .gomplateignore files from root down to file dir
	// Collect ignore files along path
	parts := strings.Split(rel, "/")
	// check root then each subdir (excluding filename)
	dirs := []string{rootAbs}
	cur := rootAbs
	for _, part := range parts[:len(parts)-1] {
		cur = filepath.Join(cur, part)
		dirs = append(dirs, cur)
	}
	// Also check parent directories above root? Docs: when processing sub-directories, .gomplateignore files in parent dir are also considered.
	// Parent of root is included if inputDir is a subdir? We'll include immediate parent chain up to cwd? Simplification: if a .gomplateignore exists in cwd parent of root and root is under it, patterns relative to that location.
	// For now only within root.
	ignored := false
	for i, dir := range dirs {
		ignorePath := filepath.Join(dir, ".gomplateignore")
		b, err := os.ReadFile(ignorePath)
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		// Path relative to this dir
		relToDir := strings.Join(parts[i:], "/")
		for _, line := range strings.Split(string(b), "\n") {
			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
			if line == "" || strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") {
				continue
			}
			neg := false
			if strings.HasPrefix(line, "!") {
				neg = true
				line = line[1:]
			}
			// gitignore dir pattern ending /
			isDirPat := strings.HasSuffix(line, "/")
			pat := strings.TrimSuffix(line, "/")
			matched := matchPattern(pat, relToDir)
			if !matched && isDirPat {
				// match any parent dir of relToDir
				segs := strings.Split(relToDir, "/")
				for j := 1; j < len(segs); j++ {
					if matchPattern(pat, strings.Join(segs[:j], "/")) {
						matched = true
						break
					}
				}
			}
			if matched {
				ignored = !neg
			}
		}
		_ = full
	}
	return ignored
}

// doublestarMatch implements ** glob
func doublestarMatch(pattern, name string) bool {
	// Use path.Match for non-** patterns segment-wise
	patParts := strings.Split(pattern, "/")
	nameParts := strings.Split(name, "/")
	return matchParts(patParts, nameParts)
}

func (r *dsRegistry) readS3(ctx context.Context, ds config.DataSource, sp fsSplit, finalURL *url.URL) (*rawResult, error) {
	// s3 FS open wraps as open: open bucket: <region error> for region failures
	q := finalURL.Query()
	region, err := awsRegion(ctx, q)
	if err != nil {
		bucket := finalURL.Host
		return nil, fsErr("open", sp, fmt.Errorf("open: open %s: %w", bucket, err))
	}
	bucket := finalURL.Host
	key := sp.name
	if key == "." {
		key = ""
	}
	endpoint := q.Get("endpoint")
	if endpoint == "" {
		endpoint = os.Getenv("AWS_S3_ENDPOINT")
	}
	disableSSL := q.Get("disableSSL") == "true"
	forcePath := q.Get("s3ForcePathStyle") == "true"
	anon := os.Getenv("AWS_ANON") == "true"
	creds := getAWSCreds()
	if anon {
		creds = awsCreds{}
	}
	isDir := strings.HasSuffix(finalURL.Path, "/") || key == ""
	mkURL := func(k string, query string) string {
		scheme := "https"
		if disableSSL {
			scheme = "http"
		}
		if endpoint != "" {
			ep := endpoint
			if !strings.Contains(ep, "://") {
				ep = scheme + "://" + ep
			}
			ep = strings.TrimSuffix(ep, "/")
			if forcePath {
				return ep + "/" + bucket + "/" + k + query
			}
			// if endpoint is custom, path style is common; use path if endpoint host is localhost etc, else virtual
			return ep + "/" + bucket + "/" + k + query
		}
		if forcePath {
			return fmt.Sprintf("%s://s3.%s.amazonaws.com/%s/%s%s", scheme, region, bucket, k, query)
		}
		return fmt.Sprintf("%s://%s.s3.%s.amazonaws.com/%s%s", scheme, bucket, region, k, query)
	}
	if isDir {
		prefix := key
		listURL := mkURL("", "?list-type=2&prefix="+url.QueryEscape(prefix))
		req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "GET", listURL, nil)
		signV4(req, nil, "s3", region, creds)
		resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fsErr("open", sp, fmt.Errorf("open: %w", err))
		}
		defer resp.Body.Close()
		b, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
		if resp.StatusCode < 200 || resp.StatusCode >= 300 {
			return nil, fsErr("open", sp, fmt.Errorf("open: %s", string(b)))
		}
		var list struct {
			Contents []struct {
				Key string `xml:"Key"`
			} `xml:"Contents"`
		}
		if err := xml.Unmarshal(b, &list); err != nil {
			return nil, fsErr("open", sp, err)
		}
		seen := map[string]bool{}
		var entries []string
		for _, c := range list.Contents {
			rel := strings.TrimPrefix(c.Key, prefix)
			first := strings.Split(rel, "/")[0]
			if first != "" && !seen[first] {
				seen[first] = true
				entries = append(entries, first)
			}
		}
		sort.Strings(entries)
		return &rawResult{isDir: true, entries: entries}, nil
	}
	getURL := mkURL(key, "")
	req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "GET", getURL, nil)
	signV4(req, nil, "s3", region, creds)
	resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fsErr("open", sp, fmt.Errorf("open: %w", err))
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
